originality.rationale: The earliest identified exact-object account is the September 11, 2014 MathOverflow question; its later October 5, 2014 answer reports the deletion h-vector only. Earl–Vander Meulen–Van Tuyl, arXiv:1505.02837v1 Theorem 6.1(iii) computes the same deletion f/h-vectors and establishes shellability of the whole complex, but does not imply whether the deletion has one or two second homology generators or its integral homotopy type. The explicit acyclic Morse reduction resolves that missing attaching map; the link map is then primitive via the exact sequence. The 2015 lexicographical-product paper does not contain this local integral homotopy computation. Actual subject and equivalent-formulation searches did not identify coverage; priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The first published shellable but non-vertex-decomposable well-covered circulant is a canonical minimal non-Cohen–Macaulay vertex-deletion test case. A precise integral homotopy classification of every deletion explains the previously recorded local obstruction, and the primitive inclusion identifies how two link classes reduce to one persistent deletion class. The exact signed attaching map is not a routine face-vector consequence and is materially informative for local elimination and graph independence topology.
